expected.notes: Today is Thu 19 Nov 2026 and pay is the last Friday, so payday is Fri 27 Nov (8 days away): the window is days 0 to 7 (19 to 26 Nov), and anything dated on payday belongs to the next period. Harbour Current (the only account) holds 34.89. Its payments in the window: HOMEBRIDGE HOUSING 77.91 on Mon 23 Nov (day 4). One predicted credit, 649.59 on Thu 26 Nov (day 7), seen twice at equal amounts a month apart, so predicted and attributed to the account. G479 (Kevin 2026-11-19, option A): Left to spend is what can be spent without any payment failing. Each counted current account contributes its LOWEST balance before payday (the lowest running balance after any of its payments, or its closing balance if that is lower, or its overdraft), money in counted only from its expected date; a dip below zero is a shortfall and reduces the total, never floored away (contribution = max(0, figure), uncovered shortfall = max(0, -figure), the total is their signed sum). Walk: 34.89 - 77.91 = -43.02 on 23 Nov (the bill bounces), then + 649.59 = 606.57 on 26 Nov. The lowest balance is -43.02, so the account contributes 0 and is 43.02 short; Left to spend is -43.02 (short), not the 606.57 the old closing-figure rule gave. The headline names it: 43.02 rounds to 43, 649.59 to about 650: '£43 short on 23 Nov, before about £650 is expected on 26 Nov'. The cover engine's own walk agrees the account is short (low point -43.02) and, with its credit, closes at 606.57 (after payments); no other account can cover it, so no move; at risk 1 (the 23 Nov payment).
